prompt: Some people say government should give health care the first priorities, some others believe education is more important priorities to spend the taxpayers' money. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
essay:
These days, people argue about the government’s priority of budget spending in healthcare or education. In my opinion, healthcare should take precedence over education.  This is because physical well-being is vital for daily productivity, and balanced nutrition is essential for students to remain attentive at school. This essay will discuss both of the arguments in detail.

On the one hand, the primary reason why I support healthcare access priority is that physical health plays a vital role in supporting human daily activities. Specifically, individuals frequently fall ill due to demanding daily routines and require prompt recovery. Comprehensive medical access – including hospitals, pharmacies, and nutritious food – is imperative to safeguard public well-being. Furthermore, healthcare initiatives are essential to improve students’ concentration in class. In many developed nations, governments are even held responsible for ensuring that learners receive adequate nutrition. Consequently, it is evident that authorities must strengthen healthcare systems to enhance the overall quality of life.

On the other hand, some people argue that education should receive more priority than healthcare. Education plays a pivotal role in expanding employment opportunities. For example, well-educated individuals are equipped to establish their own businesses, thereby generating job opportunities for others. Consequently, this alleviates national unemployment. For these reasons, the perspective that educational investment should take precedence remains widely supported.

In conclusion, while there are some arguments against greater healthcare priority, I believe that physical health and balanced nutrition make it highly beneficial for the country. Therefore, I recommended that authorities prioritise investment in healthcare over education.
